pull.title: test: Remove `BOOST_FAIL` and add info in descriptor_tests
pull.body:
The `BOOST_FAIL` here is used to exit the test based on a condition, but we can use `REQUIRE` directly. The context string is only printed on failure to my knowledge and this is not called on a child thread so there is no behavior change.

The `descriptor_tests` uses `BOOST_TEST_INFO` to add the descriptor if the next condition fails, but there are some other places that also print the public or private descriptor. Seems useful throughout this whole funciton body to attach the private and public descriptor as context.

Found in #35713 as low usage macros

ref:
- https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/latest/libs/test/doc/html/boost_test/utf_reference/testout_reference/test_output_macro_info.html
- https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/latest/libs/test/doc/html/boost_test/utf_reference/testout_reference/test_output_macro_context_sticky.html
- https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/latest/libs/test/doc/html/boost_test/utf_reference/testing_tool_ref/assertion_boost_fail.html

Seems fine to change `BOOST_FAIL` to `BOOST_REQUIRE_MESSAGE`.

I think the `BOOST_TEST_INFO` addition is not necessary, but also won't hurt so fine with me.
Left a few suggestions to extend descriptor context to the parsing checks and simplify assertions.

ACK 6fe87a36e7d23a50b1155bc267786985acf23d5a

My previous quick review turned out to be a bit shallow: the new scoped context correctly covers the removed failure info. [The `ScriptSize()` suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36772/changes#r4479530524) still stands, but it's just a nit. If you touch this again, moving `INFO_SCOPE` above the `Parse` calls would be useful too, though the current version already preserves the existing failure context.

comments.body:
Changing `BOOST_CHECK_MESSAGE` to remove failure context is surprising in a PR framed around removing `BOOST_FAIL` and adding info.

To include the parsing checks in the context too, we could wrap the whole `DoCheck` body in `BOOST_TEST_CONTEXT("Priv desc: " << prv, "Pub desc: " << pub)`.

These are in the scope of `BOOST_TEST_INFO_SCOPE` above so both descriptors are printed on failure. The `prv` addition would be redundant in this line but I can move the `INFO_SCOPE` above the `Parse` if you prefer.

The `!` is implicitly casting the `int` to a bool on the RHS so removing `!(...)` and using `NE` doesn't have the same behavior if I replaced it with `flags & SIGNABLE_FAILS`. I can replace it with `bool(flags & SIGNABLE_FAILS)` to use `NE` but not sure if that makes things any simpler
You're right, having clean bools on both sides is simpler, please resolve
